mechanism: Weekend price discovery in crypto perps happens on a structurally thinner book with the US institutional/ETF channel closed: Kraken XBT/USD hourly data 2016-2025 (87,672 obs) shows the weekend-to-weekday volatility ratio fell to 0.60 (2024) / 0.64 (2025) and the volume ratio to 0.43 / 0.46, while the nine US hours 13:00-21:59 UTC now carry 50.6% of daily realized variance (cryptoslate.com Wall-Street-time article, opened); weekend BTC-USDT spreads widen from 0.012% to 0.028% and volume drops 20-40% (dailycoin.com, opened); weekend share of BTC volume is down to 16-17% from 24% in 2018 and ~47% of volume sits in the US weekday session (investinglive.com citing Kaiko, opened). So a LARGE weekend move (>= 5% from the Friday 21:00 UTC CME close to Monday 00:00 UTC) is produced by a small set of leveraged crypto-native perp traders and liquidation engines pushing through a book roughly half as deep as a weekday book, with no ETF creation/redemption, no CME arbitrage and no institutional dealer inventory to absorb it. When the deep-liquidity participants return Monday (CME reopens Sunday 22:00 UTC, US ETF/AP channel 13:30 UTC Monday), the marginal price is re-set by a much larger, price-insensitive-to-weekend-narrative capital pool, and the thin-book overshoot component of the weekend move is given back over the Monday-Tuesday sessions. The trade fades the weekend move at the Monday 00:00 UTC open with a maker limit, symmetric 200 bps TP/SL, max hold 48 hourly bars (through Tuesday 23:00 UTC), on 18 long_1h symbols. Horizon is multi-day (hold > 8h; 6 funding settlements crossed); the 5-min poller trivially hits a fixed 00:00 UTC Monday entry and the 48h hold tolerates Mac sleep.
counterparty: Two counterparties who must pay. (1) Weekend leveraged perp traders (and the exchange liquidation engines that close them) who moved price >= 5% into a book with ~0.43-0.46x weekday volume and ~2x weekday spreads: they hold positions marked at a thin-book price and, when Monday's deep liquidity reprices the asset, their late-weekend chasers are the ones who must exit at a loss or get liquidated into the reversal -- they paid a thin-book overshoot premium that the Monday book does not honour. (2) Monday-returning institutional / ETF-channel capital, which cannot transact on Saturday-Sunday by construction (US ETFs and CME are closed) and therefore supplies the counter-flow at Monday prices, not weekend prices. The fader is paid the difference between the weekend thin-book print and the Monday deep-book print. Nobody in this chain can choose to act on Saturday: the closure is a contract/venue rule, which is why the flow is structurally forced onto Monday.
prediction: Falsifiable: on the long_1h train era, at every Sunday 23:00 UTC bar where close(Sun 23:00)/close(Fri 20:00) - 1 is >= +5% (short) or <= -5% (long), entering at the Monday 00:00 UTC open against the weekend move with 200/200 bps TP/SL and a 48-bar max hold yields n >= 30, net_bps_mean > 0 after c = 11.5 bps with bootstrap CI95 (research.swarm.lib.bootstrap_ci.mean_ci) excluding 0, and observed WR >= fee_math.p_star(200) = 0.52875 (research/swarm/runs/2026-09-17-0732/theses/session_calendar_weekend_thinbook_fade.sanity_train.txt). If weekend moves instead continue into Monday (the 'ETF holders chase the gap' alternative), net_bps_mean will be <= 0 and the thesis is dead. Secondary, NOT a pass criterion: the reversal should be larger for weekend rallies than for weekend dumps only if short-side liquidations dominate; the exploratory probe suggests the opposite (long side stronger), which the audit should report but not select on.

nearest_dead_rows.why_different: Row 7's CME-gap-fill was a BTC-only bet that price returns to the Friday CME settlement level regardless of gap size, found 'backwards' on this account's 2026 data; its 'Saturday alt strength' and 'weekend boost' were UNCONDITIONAL day-of-week longs. This thesis has no level target and no unconditional calendar drift: it fires only on the extreme tail (>= 5% weekend move, ~3.3 sym-weekends/week out of ~18 candidates) on 18 symbols, with a fixed 200 bps TP/SL rather than a fill-the-gap exit, and its mechanism is thin-book overshoot vs deep-book repricing, not 'the gap fills'. The exploratory dose-response (sign-adjusted 48h forward return flat for moves < 3%, negative only for >= 5%, research/swarm/runs/2026-09-17-0732/exploratory/session_calendar/probe_weekend_gap.out.txt) is exactly what row 7's unconditional test would average away.

Row 76 killed generic multi-day mean reversion and the 21-23 UTC overnight window as post-2022 dead via web sweep. This is not generic mean reversion of any N-day move: the conditioning variable is the venue-closure window (Fri 21:00 -> Mon 00:00 UTC), where the counterparty is defined by a contractual inability to trade, and the same 5% move Tuesday->Thursday is NOT a signal. The mechanism is liquidity-regime switching at a calendar boundary, not statistical mean reversion.

Row 6 faded a single high-volatility 5m/1h liquidation bar and found continuation. Here the fade is not of a volatility bar but of a 51-hour cumulative move measured across the weekend closure, entered only once the deep-liquidity regime resumes (Monday 00:00 UTC), i.e. after the liquidation engine's window in the thin book has ended -- row 6 entered while the cascade was still in the same liquidity regime.

Row 3 was a 1h vol-expansion fade whose OOS edge was a single-split artifact. This thesis does not condition on volatility expansion at all (a 5% weekend move on low weekend volume is by the sources a LOW-volume event, weekend vol ratio 0.60); the conditioning is calendar/venue closure, and the exploratory read reports per-weekend clustering explicitly so the audit can test the split-dependence row 3 died of.

Row 18 rejected unconditional seasonality/weekend effects (adj-R2 <= 0.002). Consistent with that, the exploratory probe shows near-zero forward return for ordinary weekends (|move| < 3%: n=311, means -3 to +22 bps, CI spanning 0); the thesis lives only in the >= 5% tail, which a seasonality regression on all weekends cannot see.
Row 67 tested day-of-week/hour gates as filters on the existing scalper books' entries. This is a standalone multi-day event trade with its own entry and exit, not a gate on another book.
Row 13 is BTC 28d time-series momentum on daily bars. This bets AGAINST the short-horizon move, only on a calendar-defined window, on alts; the sign and the conditioning are both different.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np


def signals(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """session_calendar_weekend_thinbook_fade — closed 1h bars only.
    At the bar stamped Sunday 23:00 UTC (the last bar of the weekend, closing Monday 00:00 UTC),
    measure the weekend move as close(Sun 23:00) / close(Fri 20:00) - 1, where the Fri 20:00 bar
    (closing 21:00 UTC = CME close) sits exactly 51 hourly bars earlier. If the move is >= +5%
    emit -1 (fade the thin-book weekend rally); if <= -5% emit +1 (fade the weekend dump).
    Entry is at Monday 00:00 UTC open. Uses only shift(+51) and the bar's own index; no future bars.
    A missing/irregular 51-bar gap (data hole) disables the bar."""
    c = df["close"].astype(float)
    idx = df.index
    is_sun23 = (idx.dayofweek == 6) & (idx.hour == 23)
    gap_ok = (idx.to_series().diff(51) == pd.Timedelta(hours=51)).to_numpy()
    wk = (c / c.shift(51) - 1.0).to_numpy()
    sig = pd.Series(0, index=idx, dtype="int64")
    ok = is_sun23 & gap_ok & ~np.isnan(wk)
    sig[ok & (wk >= 0.05)] = -1
    sig[ok & (wk <= -0.05)] = 1
    return sig
